It is not an overly common name, but it is often given to babies as a symbol of hope, joy, and light. The radiant and bright meaning of the name reflects the parents' vision of their child's future and their desire for the child to be a beacon of positivity and prosperity. The name may also be associated with the Islamic belief in the Day of Judgment when the sun will shine bright and all will be revealed.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Khawar" holds a significant spiritual meaning for those who hold Islamic beliefs. It is rooted in the Quranic concept of the divine light, also known as "noor." The word "Khawar" echoes the idea of the divine light that illuminates the world and guides humans towards the path of righteousness. In Islamic teachings, the name is believed to bring companionship with the divine and instills a sense of reassurance that light will always overcome darkness. It is a reminder of the divine guidance and support that individuals can rely on during their spiritual journey.
